subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals for NeuResolve
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Shah <samir@neuresolve.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals for NeuResolve

Samir, Lena —

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you mentioned, and proposed next steps. I put Vivek (solutions) and Rafael (commercial) on copy so they have context.

Call highlights / pain: 
- High token spend for inference traffic with unpredictable latency on spikes (affects SLAs for triage workflows).
- No centralized observability for model-level regressions or prompt-level degradation (multiple teams rely on different ad-hoc dashboards).
- Concerns about rolling out new model variants without clear regression signals and automated rollback.

Current stack: 
- In-house LLM routing + cache in front of hosted models (mix of cloud vendor endpoints and an open model cluster).
- Grafana for infra metrics; no structured model eval dashboards today.
- CI plays tests, but no golden prompt regression monitoring.

Success criteria (what NeuResolve needs to call this an experiment success): 
1) Clear dashboards showing per-route latency/cost and per-prompt quality trend (SLA and regression detection).
2) Golden prompt set + automated evals that surface regressions within 30 minutes of rollout.
3) Tracing hooks / request-level logs that tie tokens to traces for root-cause analysis.
4) A canary rollout guardrail and automatic fallback to previous model variant on regression.

Requested deliverables from Redwood: 
- Dashboard templates (per-route latency/cost, failure rates, prompt quality heatmap).
- Example tracing integration guide + sample trace events for our SDK.
- Eval harness for golden prompts and an initial run on your top 50 prompts.
- Suggested rollout policy (canary thresholds, rollback criteria) and alert config we can plug into PagerDuty.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Redwood provides a one-page deliverable plan (dashboards + eval plan) by EOD Fri (2026-07-24).
2) NeuResolve shares the top 50 golden prompts and a representative traffic dump (anonymized) by Wed (2026-07-28).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical session with Vivek + infra on Thu (2026-07-29) to walk through tracing hooks and data ingestion.
4) Rafael will follow up on rough pricing for a 3-month pilot by early next week.

Attachments: call notes + security questionnaire (attached).

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0199

---
Attachment: neu_resolve_call_notes.pdf (summary of meeting points)
Attachment: neuresolve-security-questions.pdf (requested security questionnaire)

From: Samir Shah <samir@neuresolve.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neuresolve.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals for NeuResolve

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap, this captures everything. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- The top 50 prompts will include a mix of short transactional prompts (~20%) and longer contextual prompts used in clinical summarization (~80%).
- For the traffic dump, we will anonymize PII but keep token/timestamp/route metadata so you can reproduce latency/cost profiles.
- Our primary success metric is prompt-quality SLAs (no more than 5% regressions post-deploy over a 7-day window) and a sub-100ms P50 latency target for the triage route.

We can get the golden prompts to you by Tue (2026-07-28). The team is comfortable with the proposed plan — please go ahead with the dashboard templates and eval harness.

Also attaching the security questionnaire; we'll expect basic SOC2 artifacts if we move to pilot.

Samir
Head of AI Ops | NeuResolve
samir@neuresolve.ai

---
Attachment: neuresolve-security-questions.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals for NeuResolve

Perfect — thanks Samir. Quick notes on follow-ups from our side: 
- Vivek will draft the tracing integration doc and a sample event schema by Thu (2026-07-23). Vivek — I added a short checklist below for the session.
- Rafael will send a pilot pricing estimate (3-month commit with reserved capacity + observability add-on) by Mon (2026-07-27).
- I'll put together the dashboard templates and the initial eval run plan and share a folder link before EOD Fri.

Vivek — suggested checklist for the technical session: 
1) What data we need to ingest for tracing (fields + retention).
2) Sample SDK snippet for emitting trace ids and token-level metadata.
3) How to map traces to dashboard metrics and golden prompt results.
4) Canary config: traffic %s, evaluation cadence, rollback thresholds.

Samir/Lena — could you confirm target attendees for the Thu session (engineer + infra + product owner)? If Thu doesn't work we can push to Fri.

I'll upload the draft dashboard templates and eval plan to the Drive link and share the HubSpot deal in a separate note.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Best,
Marissa
